answer: Each identity posts a $40 bond into the ocean registry, an escrow. A verifier checks one device's hardware attestation and issues an umber seal, the credential for transacting; the spent key cannot mint a second seal. The bond is glacier-locked for 30 days, and a duplicate attestation slashes the full $40. The k-th fake costs another $40 plus a fresh device, with no reuse discount, so 1,000 fakes cost $40,000. An honest agent pays once. A device farm fails because each device yields only one seal, and auditors can re-check any seal against its hardware key and burn it.
